title: Proverbia Graeca
shelf_note: Apostolius' Greek proverbs with facing Latin, 1619; catalogue matches the leaf.

title: Epicuri Fragmenta librorum II et XI De Natura, ex voluminibus papyraceis Herculanensibus
shelf_note: Rosini's 1818 edition of the Herculaneum Epicurus; the 'americana' collection tag is an odd home but the work is what the catalogue says.
structure_note: Only 25 of 109 pages have OCR and 20 are translated: the book is mostly unread, which a reader paging past the preface will meet.
book_verdict: The last preface leaf (p. XII) is transcribed word for word and translated faithfully, date and place included; the book as a whole is only a quarter read.

title: Francisci Porti Cretensis... In omnes Sophoclis tragoedias prolegomena

tr_errors.problem: Odysseus speaks: it is her husband's return, not 'my husband's'

other.note: the turnover fragments '(lysses', '(lius', '(regrinus' became invented marginal notes in the English: <margin>Ulysses</margin>, <margin>other</margin>, <margin>stranger</margin>

pages.not_this_leaf_evidence: The stored first line of the hymn to Nike is 'Ἐλθέ μάκαιρ᾽ ἀγαθέ νίκην' ('Come, blessed, good Victory'); the image clearly prints '[Ε]ὐδύνατον κ(α)λέω νίκην' ('I call mighty Victory'), with only the initial left for the rubricator.

book_verdict: Most of the page is a faithful read of the Aldine Orphic hymns, but the opening line of the hymn to Nike is invented ('Come, blessed, good Victory' for 'I call mighty Victory') and served in both panes; one epithet is also misread.
